safi-cedvel:1-3.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) is for interrogation. (أن) is a particle of the maṣdar (verbal noun) and of the accusative. The (الواو) in (يتركوا) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يتركوا ... ) is in the position of the accusative, standing in the place of the two objects of حسب.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يقولوا ... ) is in the position of the genitive, through an omitted lām, attached to (يتركوا) «[Note: or in the position of the genitive through an omitted bāʾ, attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the deputy agent, i.e. "holding fast to their saying: We believe".]» . (الواو) is circumstantial. (لا) is negative, and the (الواو) in (يفتنون) is the deputy agent.
The clause «حسب الناس ... » has no grammatical position; it is an opening clause (ibtidāʾiyya).
The clause «يتركوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle-type relative (أن).
The clause «يقولوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the second particle-type relative (أن).
The clause «آمنّا ... » is in the position of the accusative, being the content of what is said (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «هم لا يفتنون.» is in the position of the accusative, a ḥāl.
The clause «لا يفتنون ... » is in the position of the nominative, the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (هم).
(3) (الواو) is a conjunction. (اللام) is the lām of the oath, for an implied oath. (قد) is a particle of affirmation. (من قبلهم) is attached to an omitted ṣila of the relative. (الفاء) is a conjunction, and likewise (الواو); (اللام) is the lām of the oath for an implied oath, in both places. (يعلمنّ) is an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of the nominative. (الذين) is a relative noun, direct object, in the position of the accusative.
The clause «فتنّا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the response to the implied oath ... and the implied oath clause has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the opening clause.
The clause «يعلمنّ (the first) » has no grammatical position; it is the response to the implied oath, and the implied oath clause has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the first implied oath clause.
The clause «يعلمنّ ... (the second) » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the first clause يعلمنّ «[Note: or it is the response to the implied oath, and the oath clause is conjoined to the first oath clause.]» .

* Rhetoric:
Iltifāt (shift of address): in the words of Allah the Exalted فَلَيَعْلَمَنَّ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ صَدَقُوا وَلَيَعْلَمَنَّ الْكاذِبِينَ.
The shift to the majestic name is to instil awe, to build reverence, and to repeat the response, for added emphasis and affirmation; that is: "By Allah, His knowledge will indeed attach to the trial, an attachment in the present, by which those who were truthful in the faith they displayed are distinguished, and those who are liars in it, persisting in the lie; and their recompense of reward and punishment follows upon it."
Expression by the verbal form and the nominal form: in the words of Allah the Exalted «فَلَيَعْلَمَنَّ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ صَدَقُوا وَلَيَعْلَمَنَّ الْكاذِبِينَ» there is a contrast between the verbal form, «صدقوا», and the nominal form in His words «الكاذبين». The point of this contrast is that the active participle indicates that the verbal noun is established in the agent and firmly rooted in him, whereas the past verb does not indicate that. For at the time the verse was revealed it was a report about a people who were close to the time of their entry into Islam, and about a people persisting in disbelief; so for the former He expressed it with the verb, and for the latter with the form that indicates permanence.

* Benefits:
- Verbs of the heart.
Verbs of the heart are divided into three kinds:
a- Those that do not govern an object by themselves, and must have a preposition through which they govern, e.g. فكر في الأمر ("he reflected on the matter").
b- Those that govern one object, directly, e.g. عرف الحق ("he knew the truth") and فهم المسألة ("he understood the question").
c- Those that govern two objects directly, whose origin is a mubtadaʾ and khabar. Zufar ibn al-Ḥārith al-Kilābī says:
وكنا حسبنا كل بيضاء شحمة ... عشية لاقينا جذام وحميرا
(We had reckoned every white thing to be fat, on the evening we met Judhām and Ḥimyar.)
That is, he used to think them brave men, but they turned out to be otherwise.
And finally, we hope the meaning of the verse has become clear, namely: Do those who were quick to utter the testimony of faith consider it easy and exalt themselves over others by it, [thinking] that they will be left without being tested? Rather, Allah will try them with various kinds of trials and tribulations. For faith is not words repeated on the tongues without being supported by deeds and mingled with minds and hearts.

safi-cedvel:5-7.t:
* I'rab:
(كان) is a defective past verb, in the position of the jussive, the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ). (الفاء) is the connective of the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). (اللام) is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), for emphasis. (آت) is the khabar of inna, nominative, its sign of the nominative being the implied ḍamma on the omitted yāʾ. (الواو) is resumptive. (العليم) is a second khabar, nominative.
The clause «من كان ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «كان يرجو ... » is in the position of the nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من).
The clause «إنّ أجل الله ... » has no grammatical position; it gives the reason for the implied apodosis, i.e.: "let him prepare for it, because the term of Allah is coming".
The clause «هو السميع ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
(6) (الواو) is a conjunction. (من جاهد) is like من كان. (الفاء) is the connective of the apodosis. (إنّما) is a restrictive particle (kāffa) and what it restricts (makfūfa). (لنفسه) is attached to (يجاهد). (اللام) is the shifted lām, for emphasis. (عن العالمين) is attached to غنيّ.
The clause «من جاهد ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause من كان.
The clause «جاهد» is in the position of the nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من).
The clause «إنّما يجاهد ... » is in the position of the jussive, the apodosis, accompanied by the fāʾ.
The clause «إنّ الله لغنيّ ... » has no grammatical position; it gives a reason.
(7) (الواو) is a conjunction in the three places. (اللام) is the lām of the oath, for an implied oath. (نكفّرنّ) is an imperfect verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of the nominative, and the agent is "we", for glorification. (عنهم) is attached to (نكفّرنّ). (لنجزينّهم) is like (لنكفرنّ). (الذي) is a relative noun in the position of the genitive, a muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «الذين آمنوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause من جاهد.
The clause «آمنوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative (الذين).
The clause «عملوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause آمنوا.
The clause «نكفّرنّ ... » has no grammatical position; it is the response to the implied oath ... and the implied oath clause is in the position of the nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الذين) «[Note: or the khabar is omitted, indicated by the response to the oath.]» .
The clause «نجزينّهم ... » has no grammatical position; it is the response to the second implied oath..
The implied oath clause is in the position of the nominative, conjoined to the first oath clause.
The clause «كانوا يعملون ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative (الذي).
The clause «يعملون ... » is in the position of the accusative, the khabar of كانوا ...

safi-cedvel:4-4.t:
* I'rab:
(أم) is the disconnected (munqaṭiʿa) one, meaning بل together with the hamza, i.e. for transitional turning-away (iḍrāb) and rebuke. (أن) is a particle of the maṣdar and of the accusative.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يسبقونا) is in the position of the accusative, standing in the place of the two objects of حسب.
(ساء) is a past verb to express censure; its agent is a latent pronoun, obligatorily so, its implied form being "هو" (he). (ما) is the tamyīz (specification) of the agent «[Note: it is permissible for (ما) to be a relative noun, the agent, with the clause يحكمون as its ṣila, and the returning pronoun omitted, i.e. "they judge by it".]» . The one specified for censure (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm) is omitted, its implied form being "their judgment".
The clause «حسب الذين ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «يعملون ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative (الذين).
The clause «يسبقونا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the particle-type relative (أن).
The clause «ساء ما يحكمون.» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «يحكمون» is in the position of the accusative, an adjective (naʿt) of (ما).

safi-cedvel:8-8.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive. (بوالديه) is attached to (وصّينا). (حسنا) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar, being its adjective, with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "a bequest possessing goodness" «[Note: or a mafʿūl muṭlaq of an omitted verb standing in for the maṣdar, because it meets it in derivation, i.e.:
"Do good to them both, with goodness".]» . (الواو) is a conjunction. (جاهداك) is a past verb in the position of the jussive, the protasis. (اللام) is the lām of reason. (تشرك) is an imperfect verb, accusative through an implied أن after the lām. (بي) is attached to (تشرك). (ما) is a relative noun in the position of the accusative, direct object «[Note: or an indefinite noun with a descriptive clause, in the position of the accusative, the clause after it being its adjective]» . (لك) is attached to an omitted khabar of ليس. (به) is attached to a ḥāl from (علم) «[Note: or attached to the omitted khabar]» , and it (علم) is the postponed ism of ليس. (الفاء) is the connective of the apodosis. (لا) is a prohibitive, jussive-governing particle.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تشرك) is in the position of the genitive through the lām, attached to (جاهداك).
(إليّ) is attached to the fronted khabar of the mubtadaʾ مرجعكم. (الفاء) is a conjunction. (ما) is a particle of the maṣdar ... «[Note: or a relative noun in the position of the genitive, the returning pronoun omitted, i.e. "you used to do it"]» .
The interpreted maṣdar (ما كنتم ... ) is in the position of the genitive through the bāʾ, attached to (أنبّئكم).
The clause «وصينا ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «إن جاهداك» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the resumptive.
The clause «تشرك ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the implied particle-type relative (أن).
The clause «ليس لك به علم» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative (ما).
The clause «لا تطعهما ... » is in the position of the jussive, the apodosis, accompanied by the fāʾ.
The clause «إليّ مرجعكم ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «أنبّئكم ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause إليّ مرجعكم.
The clause «كنتم تعملون ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the particle-type relative (ما).
The clause «تعملون ... » is in the position of the accusative, the khabar of كنتم.

* Benefits:
-
It is said that Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, who was among the first to Islam, was told by his mother, Ḥamna bint Abī Sufyān: "O Saʿd, it has reached me that you have apostatised. By Allah, no roof of a house will shade me from the sun and the wind, and food and drink are forbidden to me until you disbelieve in Muḥammad." He was the dearest of her children to her. Saʿd refused, and she remained so for three days.
Then Saʿd came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and complained to him, and this verse was revealed, along with the one in Luqmān and the one in al-Aḥqāf. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded him to be gentle with her and to please her by kindness, etc. In another report, Saʿd said to her: "By Allah, if you had a hundred lives and they departed one by one, I would not disbelieve in Muḥammad; so eat if you wish, or do not eat if you wish." When she saw that, she ate.
It is also said that it was revealed about other people. There is no difference among these opinions, for the aim is one: dutifulness to parents and obedience to them, which is obligatory in Islam as long as they do not command disobedience, for there is no obedience to a created being in disobedience to the Creator.

safi-cedvel:9-9.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive. (الذين آمنوا ... لندخلنّهم) is like الذين آمنوا ... لنكفّرنّ «[Note: in verse (7) of this sūra]» in its words and clauses. (في الصالحين) is attached to (ندخلنّهم).

safi-cedvel:10-13.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive. (من الناس) is a fronted khabar for the postponed mubtadaʾ (من) «[Note: or it is an adjective of an implied mubtadaʾ, and the khabar is (من يقول), i.e. "some of the people are those who say ..."]» . (بالله) is attached to (آمنّا). (الفاء) is a conjunction, and the nāʾib fāʿil of the verb (أوذي) is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "هو" (he). (في الله) is attached to (أوذي) with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "in the path of Allah" «[Note: or (في) is causal]» . (كعذاب) is attached to a second direct object whose governor is جعل. (الواو) is a conjunction. (اللام) is the preparatory lām for an oath (muwaṭṭiʾa). (إن) is a particle of the conditional that jusses. (جاء) is a past verb in the position of the jussive, the protasis. (من ربّك) is attached to an adjective of نصر «[Note: or attached to (جاء), with من for the beginning of the range]» . (اللام) the second is the lām of the oath. (يقولن) is an imperfect verb, nominative, its sign of the nominative being the persistence of the nūn, which has been dropped because of the succession of like letters; and the (الواو), omitted because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, is the agent; and (النون) is the nūn of emphasis. (إنّا) is a particle resembling the verb, with its ism. (معكم) is an accusative adverbial, attached to the khabar of كنّا. (الهمزة) is for interrogation. (الواو) is resumptive. (أعلم) is genitive in form and accusative in position, the khabar of ليس. (ما) is a relative noun in the position of the genitive by the bāʾ, attached to أعلم. (في صدور) is attached to an omitted ṣila of ما.
The clause: «من الناس من يقول ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «يقول ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative (من).
The clause «آمنّا ... » is in the position of the accusative, the content of what is said.
The clause «أوذي ... » is in the position of the genitive, a muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «جعل ... » has no grammatical position; it is the apodosis of a non-jussive conditional.
The clause «إن جاء نصر ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the resumptive.
The clause «يقولنّ ... » has no grammatical position; it is the response to the oath ... and the apodosis is omitted, indicated by the response to the oath.
The clause «إنّا كنّا ... » is in the position of the accusative, the content of what is said.
The clause «كنّا ... معكم ... » is in the position of the nominative, the khabar of inna.
The clause «أو ليس الله بأعلم ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive, or parenthetical.
(11) (الواو) is a conjunction. (ليعلمنّ الله المنافقين): the i'rab of its like has already been given «[Note: in verse (3) of this sūra]» , word by word and clause by clause.
(12) (الواو) is a conjunction. (للذين) is attached to (قال). (الواو) is a conjunction. (اللام) is the lām of command. (الواو) the second is parenthetical. (ما) is negative, working like ليس. (حاملين) is genitive in form and accusative in position, the khabar of ما. (من خطاياهم) is attached to a ḥāl from (شيء). (شيء) is genitive in form and accusative in position, the direct object of the active participle حاملين. (اللام) is the shifted lām, for emphasis.
The clause «قال الذين ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the resumptive.
The clause «كفروا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative (الذين).
The clause «آمنوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the second relative (الذين).
The clause «اتّبعوا ... » is in the position of the accusative, the content of what is said.
The clause «لنحمل ... » is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the clause of the content of what is said.
The clause «ما هم بحاملين ... » has no grammatical position; it is parenthetical.
The clause «إنّهم لكاذبون ... » has no grammatical position; it gives a reason, or is an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī). (13) (الواو) is a conjunction. (اللام) is the lām of the oath, for an implied oath. (يحملنّ) is like يقولنّ «1». (مع) is an accusative adverbial attached to an adjective of أثقال. (يسألنّ) is like يقولنّ «2», and the omitted (الواو) in it is the nāʾib fāʿil. (يوم) is an accusative adverb of time attached to (يسألنّ). (عما) is attached to (يسألنّ) «[Note: (ما) is a maṣdar particle or a relative noun with the returning pronoun omitted.]» ...
The clause «يحملنّ ... » has no grammatical position; it is the response to the implied oath ...
The implied oath clause has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause قال الذين ...
The clause «يسألنّ ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause of the response to the oath.
The clause «كانوا يفترون ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative (ما), whether particle-type or noun.
The clause «يفترون ... » is in the position of the accusative, the khabar of كانوا.

* Morphology:
(حاملين) is the plural of حامل, an active participle from the triliteral حمل, of the pattern فاعل, with the plural فاعلين.

* Benefits:
- It is rare for the lām of command and the lā of prohibition to enter upon a single, known first-person speaker; if the speaker is more than one, their entry upon him is easier, as in the poet's words:
إذا ما خرجنا من دمشق فلا نعد ... لها أبدا ما دام فيها الجراضم
(When we have left Damascus, let us never return to it, so long as the gluttons are in it.)
And as occurs in the verse mentioned: «وَلْنَحْمِلْ خَطاياكُمْ».

safi-cedvel:14-15.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive. (اللام) is the lām of the oath, for an implied oath. (قد) is a particle of affirmation. (إلى قومه) is attached to (أرسلنا). (الفاء) is a conjunction in both places. (فيهم) is attached to (لبث). (ألف) is an accusative adverb of time attached to (لبث). (سنة) is a genitive muḍāf ilayhi. (إلّا) is a particle of exception. (خمسين) is accusative as the excepted, its sign of the accusative being the yāʾ, as it is attached to the sound masculine plural. (عاما) is an accusative tamyīz. (الواو) is the wāw of ḥāl.
The clause «أرسلنا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the response to the implied oath.
The clause «لبث ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause of the response to the oath.
The clause «أخذهم الطوفان ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to an implied one, i.e. "they denied him, so the flood seized them..".
The clause «هم ظالمون ... » is in the position of the accusative, a ḥāl.
(15) (الفاء) is a conjunction, and likewise (الواو) in both places, or the wāw of ḥāl in the second. (أصحاب) is conjoined to the object pronoun in (أنجيناه). (آية) is a second direct object whose governor is جعلناها. (للعالمين) is attached to an adjective of آية.
The clause «أنجيناه ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause أخذهم الطوفان.
The clause «جعلناها ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause أنجيناه «[Note: or it is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, with an implied قد]» .

* Rhetoric:
The point of the number: in the words of Allah the Exalted فَلَبِثَ فِيهِمْ أَلْفَ سَنَةٍ إِلَّا خَمْسِينَ عاماً.
Someone may say: why was it not said "nine hundred and fifty years"? The answer: what Allah has stated is the more judicious. For had it been said "nine hundred and fifty years", it might be supposed that this number is applied to most of that period; and this supposition is removed when it comes in this way, as if it had been said "nine hundred and fifty years, complete and full in number". Besides, this is more concise, sweeter in expression and fuller in benefit. And in it is another point:
It is that the story is told to mention what Nūḥ, peace be upon him, was tried with from his community and the long perseverance he endured, as consolation for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; so mentioning the round number is more effective and better conveys the aim, by making the listener feel the length of the time of his patience.

safi-cedvel:41-41.t:
* I'rab:
(من دون) is attached to an omitted second direct object (mafʿūl bihi), the operative governing it being (اتّخذوا). (كمثل) is attached to the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (مثل). (الواو) is circumstantial (ḥāl). (اللام) is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa) of emphasis. (لو) is a non-jussive conditional particle.
The clause «مثل الذين ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause «اتّخذوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
And the clause «اتّخذت ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī) [Note: or a ḥāl (circumstantial) from (العنكبوت), according to those who permit a ḥāl to come from the muḍāf ilayhi, with an implied (قد).].
And the clause «إنّ أوهن البيوت ... » is in the position of accusative, a ḥāl [Note: it may be resumptive, in which case it has no position.].
And the clause «لو كانوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive ... and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, its implied form being "ما عبدوا الأصنام".
And the clause «يعلمون ... » is in the position of accusative, the khabar of (كانوا).

* Morphology:
(العنكبوت) is a generic noun (ism jins) for the well-known animal; its wazn is فعللوت, so the wāw and the tāʾ are augmentative. Its plural is عناكب and عناكيب [Note: and some have added عكاب, عكبة and أعكب.]. It may be masculine or feminine, and عنكبوت may refer to the singular and the plural alike.
(أوهن) is an elative (ism tafḍīl) from the triliteral (وهن); its wazn is أفعل.

* Rhetoric:
The composite simile (al-tashbīh al-murakkab): in the saying of Allah the Exalted مَثَلُ الَّذِينَ اتَّخَذُوا مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ أَوْلِياءَ كَمَثَلِ الْعَنْكَبُوتِ اتَّخَذَتْ بَيْتاً وَإِنَّ أَوْهَنَ الْبُيُوتِ لَبَيْتُ الْعَنْكَبُوتِ.
The meaning: the likeness of those who took protectors besides Allah, in that which they took as a support and reliance in their religion and took as patrons besides Allah the Exalted, is like the spider in what it has woven and taken as a house. The purpose is to establish [the weakness of] their religious affair, and that it has reached the utmost limit beyond which there is no further limit. The pivot of the simile is that their protectors are in the position of what the spider weaves: weak in condition and unfit to be relied upon. On this basis, His saying «إِنَّ أَوْهَنَ الْبُيُوتِ ... » is an appended conclusion (tadhyīl) which confirms the purpose of the simile.
It is also possible that the meaning and the purpose of the simile are as you have heard, except that the tadhyīl is made a representative metaphor (istiʿāra tamthīliyya), and what precedes is like a preamble to it.

* Benefits:
- Returning to the parable and the representation (al-mathal wa-l-tamthīl) in the Noble Qur'an: although we have drawn attention to this noble art many times. Some of the scholars of rhetoric considered it part of the representative metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-tamthīliyya) founded on the representative simile (al-tashbīh al-tamthīlī). ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī said: Do you doubt that representation works like magic in joining things that differ, so that the distance between east and west is shortened? It shows you the meanings represented in standing figures, makes the mute speak for you, gives you eloquence from the inarticulate, shows you life in inanimate things, shows you the very union of opposites, and makes a thing both near and far at once.
Thus a number of the ancients perceived the distinction that representation has in the Noble Qur'an.

safi-cedvel:42-42.t:
* I'rab:
(ما) is negative [Note: or an interrogative noun in the position of accusative, a direct object (mafʿūl bihi) whose operative is (يدعون), and (من شيء) is the tamyīz (specification) of (ما).]. (من دونه) is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from (شيء). (شيء) is genitive in form and accusative in position, a direct object whose operative is (يدعون). (الواو) is a conjunction. (الحكيم) is a second khabar (predicate), nominative ...
And the clause «إنّ الله يعلم ... » has no grammatical position; it is causal.
And the clause «يعلم ... » is in the position of nominative, the khabar of (إنّ).
And the clause «ما يدعون ... » is in the position of accusative, a direct object of the verb of knowing, which is suspended (muʿallaq) by the negation.
And the clause «هو العزيز ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause «إنّ الله يعلم».

safi-cedvel:43-43.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is a conjunction. (الأمثال) is a badal (substitute) for the demonstrative noun, or an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) to it, nominative. (للناس) is attached to (نضربها). (الواو) is a conjunction. (ما) is negative. (إلّا) is for restriction. (العالمون) is the fāʿil (agent), nominative, its sign of nominative case being the wāw.
The clause «تلك الأمثال نضربها ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause «مثل الذين» [Note: in verse (41) of this sūra.].
And the clause «نضربها للناس ... » is in the position of nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (تلك).
And the clause «ما يعقلها إلّا العالمون ... » is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause «نضربها».

safi-cedvel:44-44.t:
* I'rab:
(بالحقّ) is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the Name of Majesty (Allah), and the bāʾ denotes accompaniment. (في ذلك) is attached to an omitted khabar of (إنّ). (اللام) is the lām of commencement (lām al-ibtidāʾ), for emphasis. (آية) is the ism (noun) of (إنّ), accusative. (للمؤمنين) is attached to an adjective (naʿt) of (آية).
The clause «خلق الله ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause «إنّ في ذلك لآية ... » has no grammatical position; it is causal, or an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).

safi-cedvel:45-45.t:
* I'rab:
(ما) is a relative noun in the position of accusative, a direct object; and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of the verb (أوحي) is a latent pronoun (ḍamīr mustatir), its implied form being "هو" (he), and it is the returning pronoun (al-ʿāʾid). (إليك) is attached to (أوحي). (من الكتاب) is attached to (أوحي) [Note: or attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the latent pronoun in (أوحي).]. (الواو) is a conjunction in the three places. (عن الفحشاء) is attached to (تنهى). (اللام) is the lām of commencement, for emphasis. (ما) is a maṣdar particle [Note: or a relative noun in the position of accusative, the returning pronoun being omitted, i.e. "تصنعونه".] ...
The clause «اتل ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause «أوحي إليك ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (ما).
And the clause «أقم ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the resumptive clause.
And the clause «إنّ الصلاة تنهى ... » has no grammatical position; it is causal.
And the clause «تنهى عن الفحشاء ... » is in the position of nominative, the khabar of (إنّ). [Translator's note: the source reads «في محلّ لها رفع», with a stray «لها»; evidently «في محلّ رفع» is meant.]
And the clause «ذكر الله أكبر ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the causal clause.
And the clause «الله يعلم ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the causal clause.
And the clause «يعلم ما تصنعون ... » is in the position of nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الله).
And the clause «تصنعون ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the particle-type maṣdar (ما).
And the interpreted maṣdar (ما تصنعون) is in the position of accusative, a direct object whose operative is (يعلم).

* Morphology:
(أقم) involves ʿilāl (weak-letter alteration) by elision, owing to the construction on sukūn. Its origin is أقيم (with fatḥa on the hamza); the yāʾ came quiescent next to the mīm, so the yāʾ was dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, and it became أقم, its wazn being أفل. This is the way of the hollow (al-muʿtall al-ajwaf) verb in the imperative. The yāʾ is the ʿayn of the word, converted from a wāw.
(تنهى) involves ʿilāl by conversion; its origin is تنهي: the yāʾ came vowelled after a fatḥa and was converted into an alif. It has been written with an undotted yāʾ because it is fourth [in the radicals].

safi-cedvel:46-46.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive. (لا) is the prohibitive lā, which jusses. (إلّا) is for restriction. (بالتي) is attached to (تجادلوا), i.e. "with the disputation which ...". (إلّا) is for exception. (الذين) is a relative noun in the position of accusative, as the excepted. (منهم) is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of (ظلموا). (الواو) is a conjunction in the four places. (بالذي) is attached to (آمنّا); and the nāʾib fāʿil of the verb (أنزل) is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "هو" (he), and it is the returning pronoun. (إلينا) is attached to (أنزل), and likewise (إليكم) is attached to the second [(أنزل)]. (له) is attached to (مسلمون).
The clause «لا تجادلوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause «هي أحسن ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (التي).
And the clause «ظلموا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
And the clause «قولوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the resumptive clause.
And the clause «آمنا ... » is in the position of accusative, the content of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
And the clause «أنزل إلينا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الذي).
And the clause «أنزل إليكم ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause «أنزل إلينا».
And the clause «إلهنا وإلهكم واحد ... » is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the content of the saying.
And the clause «نحن له مسلمون ... » is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the content of the saying.

safi-cedvel:47-49.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive. (كذلك) is attached to an omitted absolute object (mafʿūl muṭlaq) whose operative is (أنزلنا). (إليك) is attached to (أنزلنا). (الفاء) is a conjunction of consequence (ʿāṭifa tafrīʿiyya).
(الكتاب) is a second direct object, accusative. (به) is attached to (يؤمنون). (الواو) is a conjunction. (من هؤلاء) is attached to an omitted fronted khabar (predicate) [Note: or it is an adjective (naʿt) of an omitted mubtadaʾ whose khabar is (من يؤمن به), the implied sense being: "some of these are those who believe in it", the reference being to the people of Mecca.] for the postponed mubtadaʾ, the relative noun (من). (به) is attached to (يؤمن). (الواو) is parenthetical or circumstantial (ḥāl). (ما) is negative. (بآياتنا) is attached to (يجحد). (إلّا) is for restriction.
The clause «أنزلنا ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause «الذين آتيناهم ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the resumptive clause.
And the clause «آتيناهم ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
And the clause «يؤمنون به ... » is in the position of nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الذين).
And the clause «من هؤلاء من يؤمن ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause «الذين آتيناهم».
And the clause «يؤمن به ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (من).
And the clause «يجحد ... الكافرون ... » has no grammatical position; it is parenthetical, or it is in the position of accusative, a ḥāl (circumstantial).
(48) (الواو) is a conjunction. (ما) is negative. (من قبله) is attached to (تتلو) [Note: or attached to a ḥāl from (كتاب).]. (كتاب) is genitive in form and accusative in position, a direct object. (الواو) is a conjunction. (لا) is negative. (بيمينك) is attached to (تخطّه). (إذا), with tanwīn, is a particle of response [Note: what is meant by its being "a response" is that it is a particle which accompanies the response, even though it is not what links it to the condition.]. (اللام) is the connecting lām of the apodosis of an implied condition, namely (لو) [Note: al-Farrāʾ said: wherever (إذا), with tanwīn, comes before the lām, then (لو) is implied before it if it is not overt.].
The clause «ما كنت ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause «أنزلنا».
And the clause «تتلو ... » is in the position of accusative, the khabar of (كنت).
And the clause «لا تخطّه ... » is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause «تتلو».
And the clause «ارتاب المبطلون ... » has no grammatical position; it is the apodosis of the implied condition (لو).
(49) (بل) is for transitional rejection (iḍrāb intiqālī). (في صدور) is attached to an adjective (naʿt) of (بيّنات), and the (الواو) in (أوتوا) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). (الواو) is a conjunction. (ما يجحد ... الظالمون) is like the preceding.
And the clause «هو آيات ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause «أوتوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
And the clause «ما يجحد ... إلّا الظالمون ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause «هو آيات ...».

* Rhetoric:
Iṭnāb (amplification): in the saying of Allah the Exalted وَلا تَخُطُّهُ بِيَمِينِكَ.
It is an unavoidable amplification, for the mention of the right hand, which is the limb with which writing is practised, adds a vivid depiction of what is denied of him, namely that he was a writer. Do you not see that if you said in the affirmative, "I saw the emir writing this book with his right hand", it would be stronger in establishing that he himself undertook its writing? Similar is their saying: "I saw him with my own eyes" and "I seized it with my own hand", in verifying the reality and confirming it, so that no room is left for figurative meaning. This is said of everything whose attainment is momentous and which is hard to reach. It is frequent in the Noble Qur'an.

* Benefits:
The recording of the Qur'an:
Al-Khaṭṭābī said: The Prophet ﷺ did not gather the Qur'an into a codex only because he was awaiting the revelation of an abrogating text for some of its rulings or its recitation. When its revelation ended with his death, Allah inspired the Rightly-Guided Caliphs to do it, in fulfilment of His truthful promise after him to guarantee its preservation for this community. So its beginning was at the hands of al-Ṣiddīq [Abū Bakr] on the advice of ʿUmar.
Al-Suyūṭī said: The whole Qur'an was written down in the time of the Messenger, but it was not gathered in one place, nor arranged by sūras. On the authority of Zayd ibn Thābit, who said: Abū Bakr sent for me after the killing of the people of al-Yamāma, and ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb was with him. Abū Bakr said: ʿUmar came to me and said: Killing has become intense in the battlefields, and much of the Qur'an will go. Zayd said to ʿUmar: How can you do what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not do? ʿUmar said: By Allah, this is good ...
He kept returning to me until Allah expanded my breast for that. Abū Bakr said: You are a young, intelligent man; we do not suspect you, and you used to write down the revelation for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. So seek out the Qur'an and collect it. Zayd said: By Allah, had they charged me with moving one of the mountains, it would not have been heavier on me than what he commanded me of collecting the Qur'an. I said: And Abū Bakr kept returning to me until Allah expanded my breast for that for which He had expanded the breast of Abū Bakr and ʿUmar. So I sought out the Qur'an, collecting it from palm-ribs and thin white stones [Note: al-ʿasab: plural of ʿasīb, a palm-branch whose leaves have been stripped, which was used for writing on; al-lakhāf: thin white stones, which were also used for writing on.] and from the breasts of men, until I found the end of Sūrat al-Tawba with Abū Khuzayma al-Anṣārī; I did not find it with anyone else, namely: لقد جاءكم رسول من أنفسكم عزيز عليه ما عنتم حريص عليكم بالمؤمنين, to the end of Barāʾa. And when the time of ʿUthmān came, occasions arose which called for reconsidering the matter of these leaves which Zayd ibn Thābit had written.
Al-Bukhārī related on the authority of Anas that Ḥudhayfa ibn al-Yamān came to ʿUthmān; he had been fighting alongside the people of Syria in the conquest of Armenia and Azerbaijan with the people of Iraq, and their differing in recitation alarmed Ḥudhayfa. He said to ʿUthmān: Reach this community before they differ. So ʿUthmān sent to Ḥafṣa daughter of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, wife of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: Send us these leaves, that we may copy them into codices, then we will return them to you. Ḥafṣa sent them to ʿUthmān, and he commanded Zayd ibn Thābit, ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr, Saʿīd ibn al-ʿĀṣ and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Hishām, and they copied them into codices. ʿUthmān said to the group of three Qurashīs: If you and Zayd ibn Thābit differ over anything of the Qur'an, write it in the tongue of Quraysh, for it was revealed only in their tongue. They did so, until, when they had copied the leaves into codices, ʿUthmān returned the leaves to Ḥafṣa. And ʿUthmān sent to every region a codex of what they had copied, and commanded that everything else of the Qur'an, in any leaf or codex, be burned.

safi-cedvel:50-50.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive. (لولا) is a particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ) or reproach. (عليه) is attached to (أنزل). (آيات) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). (من ربه) is attached to (أنزل) [Note: or attached to an adjective (naʿt) of (آيات).]. (إنّما) is a restraining particle together with what it restrains (kāffa wa-makfūfa). (عند) is an accusative adverb (ẓarf) attached to an omitted khabar (predicate) of (الآيات). (الواو) is a conjunction. (مبين) is an adjective (naʿt) of (نذير), nominative.
The clause «قالوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause «لولا أنزل.. آيات ... » is in the position of accusative, the content of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
And the clause «قل ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
And the clause «إنّما الآيات عند الله. is in the position of accusative, the content of the saying. [Translator's note: the closing guillemet of the clause is missing in the source.]
And the clause «إنّما أنا نذير ... » is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause that is the content of the saying.
Part Twenty-One
The remainder of Sūrat al-ʿAnkabūt
From verse 51 to verse 69. Sūrat al-Rūm, its verses 60. Sūrat Luqmān, its verses 34. Sūrat al-Sajda, its verses 30. Sūrat al-Aḥzāb, from verse 1 to verse 30.

safi-cedvel:51-51.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) is for interrogation of reproach. (الواو) is a conjunction. (أنا) is a particle resembling the verb (ḥarf mushabbah bi-l-fiʿl) and its ism (noun). (عليك) is attached to (أنزلنا). (عليهم) is attached to (يتلى). (في ذلك) is a fronted khabar (predicate). (اللام) is for emphasis. (رحمة) is the ism of (إنّ), accusative, postponed. (لقوم) is attached to (ذكرى).
And the interpreted maṣdar (أنّا أنزلنا ... ) is in the position of nominative, the fāʿil (agent) of (يكفهم).
The clause «لم يكفهم ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to an implied resumption, i.e.: "Is the revealed sign deficient, and was its revelation, recited, not sufficient for them?" [Note: it may be resumptive.]
And the clause «أنزلنا ... » is in the position of nominative, the khabar of (أنّ).
And the clause «يتلى ... » is in the position of accusative, a ḥāl (circumstantial) from (الكتاب).
And the clause «إنّ في ذلك لرحمة ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption.
And the clause «يؤمنون..» is in the position of genitive, an adjective (naʿt) of (قوم).

* Benefits:
- أَوَلَمْ يَكْفِهِمْ:
We affirm that the signs of the jussive mood (jazm) of the imperfect verb are three: sukūn for the sound verb, dropping of the nūn for the five verbs (al-afʿāl al-khamsa), and dropping of the weak letter for the verb weak in its final letter.
It is very useful to present to the reader the rule on the construction (binā') of the imperative verb, which says: the imperative verb is built on that by which its imperfect is jussive.
Since the signs of the jussive of the imperfect are three, they correspond to three cases of the construction of the imperative:
a- If it is sound in its final letter: it is built on sukūn, because its imperfect is jussive with sukūn.
b- If it is one of the five verbs, that is, if the alif of the dual, the wāw of the group or the yāʾ of the feminine addressee is attached to it: it is built on dropping of the nūn, because its imperfect is jussive with dropping of the nūn.
c- If it is weak in its final letter: it is built on dropping of the weak letter from its end, because its imperfect is jussive with dropping of the weak letter from its end.
An example of the first is اكتب; of the second «اقرءا، اكتبوا، العبي»; and of the third «اتل، ارم، اغز».
So reflect, and may you be guided to what is right.

safi-cedvel:52-52.t:
* I'rab:
(الله) the Name of Majesty is genitive in form and nominative in position, the fāʿil (agent) of (كفى). (بيني) is an accusative adverb (ẓarf) attached to (شهيدا), its sign of accusative being the implied fatḥa on the letter before the yāʾ, and (الياء) is the muḍāf ilayhi. (بينكم) is like (بيني), being conjoined to it. (شهيدا) is a tamyīz (specification), accusative [Note: or a ḥāl (circumstantial).]. (في السموات) is attached to an omitted ṣila of the relative noun (ما). (الواو) is resumptive, or a conjunction. (بالباطل) is attached to (آمنوا). (بالله) is attached to (كفروا). (أولئك) is a second mubtadaʾ (subject), in the position of nominative [Note: or a badal (substitute) for the relative noun (الذين).]. (هم) is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl) [Note: or a detached pronoun, a third mubtadaʾ whose khabar is (الخاسرون), the clause being the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (أولئك).]. (الخاسرون) is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (أولئك).
The clause «قل ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause «كفى بالله ... » is in the position of accusative, the content of the saying.
And the clause «يعلم ... » is in the position of accusative, a ḥāl (circumstantial) [Note: or it has no position, being an explanatory resumption.].
And the clause «الذين آمنوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive [Note: or conjoined to the clause that is the content of the saying, in the position of accusative.].
And the clause «آمنوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
And the clause «كفروا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the ṣila clause.
And the clause «أولئك ... الخاسرون.» is in the position of nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الذين).

* Rhetoric:
The imaginative metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-takhyīliyya): in the saying of Allah the Exalted «أُولئِكَ هُمُ الْخاسِرُونَ»:
In "loss" (al-khusrān) there is an imaginative metaphor, of which it is itself the indicator (qarīna), because loss is customary in trade. This speech came in the manner of fairness, in that He did not declare outright that they are those who believe in falsehood and disbelieve in Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, but presented it in the form of generality, so that reflection might fall upon the intended meaning. It is like His saying «وَإِنَّا أَوْ إِيَّاكُمْ لَعَلى هُدىً أَوْ فِي ضَلالٍ مُبِينٍ».

safi-cedvel:53-55.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive. (بالعذاب) is attached to (يستعجلونك). (الواو) is a conjunction. (لولا) is a non-jussive conditional particle. (أجل) is a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is omitted. (اللام) occurs in the apodosis of (لولا), and the second [lām] is the lām of an oath, for an implied oath. (يأتينّهم) is an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa, in the position of nominative; the fāʿil (agent) is "he", and (هم) is a pronoun, a direct object. (بغتة) is a maṣdar in the position of ḥāl (circumstantial) [Note: or an absolute object (mafʿūl muṭlaq) standing in for the maṣdar, because it meets the verb in meaning, i.e. "so that it takes them by surprise (ليبغتهم) with a sudden surprise".]. (الواو) is the wāw of ḥāl. (لا) is negative.
The clause «يستعجلونك ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause «لولا أجل (موجود ... ) » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the resumptive clause.
And the clause «جاءهم العذاب ... » has no grammatical position; it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
And the clause «يأتينّهم..» has no grammatical position; it is the response to the implied oath, and the implied oath clause has no grammatical position; it is resumptive, or conjoined to the resumptive clause. And the clause «هم لا يشعرون..» is in the position of accusative, a ḥāl.
And the clause «لا يشعرون..» is in the position of nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هم).
(54) (الواو) is resumptive. (اللام) is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa) of emphasis. (بالكافرين) is attached to (محيطة).
And the clause «يستعجلونك (the second)» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive, to emphasise the first clause.
And the clause «إنّ جهنّم لمحيطة ... » has no grammatical position; it is a causal resumption.
(يوم) is an accusative adverb of time, attached to (محيطة). (من فوقهم) is attached to (يغشاهم), and likewise (من تحت) is conjoined to (من فوقهم). The fāʿil (agent) of (يقول) is omitted, referring to the one charged with the punishment, understood from the context. (ما) is a relative noun in the position of accusative, a direct object, with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "the recompense of what you used to ...". And the returning pronoun is omitted, i.e. "تعملونه".
And the clause «يغشاهم ... » is in the position of genitive, a muḍāf ilayhi.
And the clause «يقول ... » is in the position of genitive, conjoined to the clause «يغشاهم».
And the clause «ذوقوا ... » is in the position of accusative, the content of the saying.
And the clause «كنتم تعملون..» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (ما).
And the clause «تعملون.» is in the position of accusative, the khabar of (كنتم).

* Rhetoric:
He, glory be to Him, the Exalted, singled out the fire of Hell with the two sides, the upper and the lower, and did not mention the right or the left, nor the back or the front, to show the difference between it and the fire of this world, which surrounds all sides. The fire of Hell is not extinguished by treading upon it, but it descends from above.

safi-cedvel:56-57.t:
* I'rab:
(الذين) is an indeclinable relative noun in the position of accusative, an adjective (naʿt) of (عبادي). The first (الفاء) connects the apodosis of an implied condition; the second (الفاء) is redundant, for embellishment. (إياي) is a detached pronoun in the position of accusative, a direct object of an omitted verb which what follows explains. The (النون) in (اعبدون) is the nūn of protection (wiqāya) before the omitted yāʾ, for the sake of the verse-ending (fāṣila).
The vocative clause «يا عبادي» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause «آمنوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
And the clause «إنّ أرضي واسعة..» has no grammatical position; it is the response to the vocative.
And the implied clause «(اعبدوا)..» is in the position of jussive, the apodosis of the implied condition, i.e. "if your land becomes narrow for you, then worship Me in whatever land you emigrate to other than your land".
And the clause «اعبدون..» has no grammatical position; it is explicative.
(56) (ثمّ) is a conjunction. (إلينا) is attached to (ترجعون), and the (الواو) in it is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).
And the clause «كلّ نفس ذائقة..» has no grammatical position; it is a causal resumption.
And the clause «ترجعون..» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the causal clause.

* Benefits:
- يا عِبادِيَ:
We state for the second time that the one addressed (al-munādā) is of five kinds: two of them are built on ḍamma, in the position of accusative, namely the singular proper noun, such as يا محمد and يا سميح, and the specific indefinite, such as: يا رجل and يا تلميذ.
And three are accusative: the non-specific indefinite, such as: يا رجلا and يا تلميذا; the muḍāf, such as: يا صاحب المنزل and يا أستاذ الدرس; and that resembling the muḍāf, such as: يا طالعا جبلا and يا ساكنا في الدار.

safi-cedvel:58-59.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive. (اللام) is the lām of an oath, for an implied oath. (نبوّئنّهم) is like (يأتينّهم) [Note: in verse (53) of this sūra.]. (من الجنّة) is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from (غرفا), which is a second direct object, accusative. (من تحتها) is attached to (تجري) [Note: or to an omitted ḥāl from (الأنهار).]. (خالدين) is a ḥāl from the object pronoun in (نبوّئنّهم), accusative [Note: or from (الجنّة), or from (غرفا).]. The one specified for praise (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-madḥ) is omitted, its implied form being "الجنّة" or "هذا الأجر".
The clause «الذين آمنوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause «آمنوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
And the clause «عملوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the ṣila clause.
And the clause «نبوّئنّهم ... » has no grammatical position; it is the response to the implied oath ... and the oath clause with its response is in the position of nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الذين) [Note: or the khabar is omitted, the response to the oath indicating it.].
And the clause «تجري ... » is in the position of accusative, an adjective (naʿt) of (غرفا).
And the clause «نعم أجر ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption, or causal. (59) (الذين) is a relative noun in the position of genitive, an adjective of (العاملين) [Note: or the khabar of an obligatorily omitted mubtadaʾ in the manner of praise, its implied form being "هم" (they), the clause being resumptive; or a direct object of an omitted verb, its implied form being "I praise".]. (على ربّهم) is attached to (يتوكّلون).
And the clause «صبروا....» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the second relative noun (الذين).
And the clause «يتوكّلون..» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the ṣila clause.

* Morphology:
(غرفا) is the plural of غرفة ... and see verse (75) of Sūrat al-Furqān.

safi-cedvel:60-60.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive. (كأيّن) is a noun that stands for number (ism kināya ʿan al-ʿadad), indeclinable on sukūn, in the position of nominative, a mubtadaʾ (subject). (من دابّة) is a tamyīz (specification). (لا) is negative. The first (الواو) is a conjunction, the second resumptive. (إيّاكم) is a detached pronoun in the position of accusative, conjoined to the attached pronoun in (يرزقها). (العليم) is a second khabar (predicate), nominative.
The clause «كأيّن من دابة ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause «لا تحمل..» is in the position of genitive, an adjective (naʿt) of (دابّة).
And the clause «الله يرزقها..» is in the position of nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (كأيّن).
And the clause «يرزقها..» is in the position of nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الله).
And the clause «هو السميع..» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.

* Benefits:
- «كأي» or «كأين», according to the orthography of the codex: It is a compound noun made of the kāf of comparison and the tanwīn-bearing «أي», and it is permissible to pause on it with the nūn. It has the meaning of «كم» and agrees with it in five respects:
"Vagueness, need of a tamyīz, indeclinability, obligatory precedence in the sentence, and conveying multiplicity," which is the most frequent, as in «وَكَأَيِّنْ مِنْ نَبِيٍّ قاتَلَ مَعَهُ رِبِّيُّونَ كَثِيرٌ».
And it differs from it in five respects:
First: «كأين» is compound while كم is simple.
Second: its tamyīz is mostly genitive with «من», as has just been seen.
Third: according to the majority it does not occur as interrogative.
Fourth: it does not occur in the genitive.
Fifth: its khabar does not occur as a single word but as a clause, as seen in the preceding verses.

safi-cedvel:61-61.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive. (اللام) is the lām that prepares for the oath. (سألتهم) is a past verb, indeclinable, in the position of jussive, the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ). (من) is an interrogative noun in the position of nominative, a mubtadaʾ (subject). (الواو) is a conjunction in the three places. (اللام) is the lām of an oath, for an implied oath. (يقولن) is an imperfect verb, nominative, its sign of nominative being the retention of the nūn, which has been dropped because of the succession of similar letters; and the wāw, dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, is the fāʿil (agent); and (النون) is the nūn of emphasis. (الله) the Name of Majesty is a mubtadaʾ, nominative, and the khabar (predicate) is omitted, i.e.: "Allah did that". (الفاء) connects the apodosis of an implied condition. (أنّى) is an interrogative noun in the position of accusative, an adverb of place attached to (يؤفكون), and the (الواو) in it is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).
The clause «إن سألتهم ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause «من خلق ... » is in the position of accusative, a direct object of the verb of asking, which is suspended (muʿallaq) by the interrogative (من), with an implied preposition, i.e. "about whom created ...".
And the clause «خلق....» is in the position of nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من).
And the clause «سخّر ... » is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause «خلق ...».
And the clause «يقولنّ ... » has no grammatical position; it is the response to the oath ... and the apodosis of the condition is omitted, the response to the oath indicating it.
And the clause «الله (فعل..) ..» is in the position of accusative, the content of the saying.
And the clause «يؤفكون ... » is in the position of jussive, the apodosis of an implied condition, accompanied by the fāʾ, i.e.: "if desire turns them away, then how are they turned away". And the implied protasis clause has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.

safi-cedvel:62-62.t:
* I'rab:
(لمن) is attached to (يبسط). (من عباده) is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the implied returning pronoun [Note: i.e. "whomever He wills to give provision from among His servants"; it may also be a tamyīz (specification) of the relative noun (من).]. (له) is attached to (يقدر). (بكلّ) is attached to (عليم).
The clause «الله يبسط ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause «يبسط ... » is in the position of nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الله).
And the clause «يشاء ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (من).
And the clause «يقدر له ... » is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause «يبسط».
And the clause «إنّ الله ... عليم» has no grammatical position; it is causal.

safi-cedvel:63-63.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive, or a conjunction. (لئن.. نزّل) is like (لئن.. خلق) [Note: in verse (61) of this sūra.]. (من السماء) is attached to (نزل). (الفاء) is a conjunction. (به) is attached to (أحيا). (من بعد) is attached to (أحيا). (ليقولنّ الله) is like the preceding [Note: in verse (61) of this sūra.]. (لله) is attached to the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الحمد). (بل) is for transitional rejection (iḍrāb intiqālī). (لا) is negative.
The clause «إن سألتهم ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive [Note: or conjoined to the clause «إن سألتهم» in verse (61), what lies between them being parenthetical.].
And the clause «من نزّل ... » is in the position of accusative, a direct object of the verb of asking, suspended by the interrogative (من).
And the clause «نزّل ... » is in the position of nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من).
And the clause «أحيا ... » is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause «نزّل».
And the clause «يقولنّ..» has no grammatical position; it is the response to the oath.. and the apodosis of the condition is omitted, the response to the oath indicating it.
And the clause «الله (فعل ذلك) » . is in the position of accusative, the content of the saying.
And the clause «قل ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause «الحمد لله ... » is in the position of accusative, the content of the saying.
And the clause «أكثرهم لا يعقلون..» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause «لا يعقلون..» is in the position of nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (أكثرهم).

safi-cedvel:64-64.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive. (ما) is a negative that does not operate (muhmala). (الحياة) is a badal (substitute) for the demonstrative noun, or an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition). (إلّا) is for restriction. (لهو) is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (هذه). (الواو) is a conjunction. (اللام) is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa) of emphasis. (لو) is a non-jussive conditional particle.
The clause «ما هذه.. إلّا لهو» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause «إنّ الدار ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the resumptive clause.
And the clause «هي الحيوان..» is in the position of nominative, the khabar of (إنّ).
And the clause «كانوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.. and the apodosis of the condition is omitted, its implied form being: "they would not have preferred the life of this world".
And the clause «يعلمون..» is in the position of accusative, the khabar of (كانوا)..

* Morphology:
(الحيوان) is a noun for everything that has life, whether endowed with speech or not, and in the verse it has come in the sense of the everlasting life in which there is no death..
And the (الواو) in it is converted from a yāʾ, according to Sībawayh, irregularly (shudhūdhan), lest it be confused with the dual, and it was not converted into an alif lest one of the two alifs be dropped.. According to others than Sībawayh, the wāw is original and there is no conversion.

safi-cedvel:16-18.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) a conjunction (إبراهيم) conjoined to (نوحا) «[Note: in verse (14) of this sūra, or conjoined to the pronoun object in (أنجيناه) - verse 15 - or it is a direct object of an omitted verb, its implied form being: "mention", and the conjunction becomes a conjunction of clauses.]», accusative (إذ) an adverb of past time in the position of an accusative, attached to (أرسلنا) «[Note: or attached to (أنجينا) ... or it is a badal ishtimāl (inclusive substitute) from إبراهيم if it is accusative by (اذكر).]», (لقومه) attached to (قال), (لكم) attached to خير (كنتم) a defective past verb - a naskh (abrogating) verb - in the position of a jussive, the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ).
Clause: «قال ...» is in the position of a genitive, a muḍāf ilayhi.
Clause: «اعبدوا ...» is in the position of an accusative, being the quoted speech.
Clause: «اتّقوه ...» is in the position of an accusative, conjoined to the clause اعبدوا ...
Clause: «ذلكم خير لكم ...» has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption.
Clause: «كنتم تعلمون ...» has no grammatical position; it is a resumption within the scope of the quoted speech ...
The apodosis is omitted, indicated by what precedes it.
Clause: «تعلمون ...» is in the position of an accusative, the predicate of كنتم.
(17) (إنّما) restraining and restrained (kāffa and makfūfa) (من دون) attached to a ḥāl of (أوثانا), and the second is attached to a ḥāl of the implied ʿāʾid, that is: "you worship it besides Allah" (لا) a negation (لكم) attached to a ḥāl of (رزقا), and it is a direct object, its governing word being يملكون «[Note: or it is a mafʿūl muṭlaq standing in for the maṣdar because it meets the verb in meaning, that is: "they provide for you provision".]» (الفاء) connecting the apodosis of an implied condition (عند) an accusative adverb attached to (ابتغوا), (الواو) a conjunction in both places (له) attached to (اشكروا), (إليه) attached to (ترجعون), and the wāw in it is the deputy agent.
Clause: «تعبدون ...» has no grammatical position; it is a second justification «[Note: or another resumption within the scope of the quoted speech.]».
Clause: «تخلقون ...» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause تعبدون.
Clause: «إنّ الذين تعبدون ...» has no grammatical position; it is a justification of the justification.
Clause: «تعبدون (the second)» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative (الذين).
Clause: «لا يملكون ...» is in the position of a nominative, the predicate of إنّ.
Clause: «ابتغوا ...» is in the position of a jussive, the apodosis of an implied condition, that is: "if you need something, then seek".
Clause: «اعبدوه ...» is conjoined to the clause ابتغوا ...
Clause: «اشكروا له ...» is conjoined to the clause ابتغوا..
Clause: «ترجعون ...» has no grammatical position; it is a justification.
(18) (الواو) a conjunction (الفاء) connecting the apodosis (قد) a particle of certainty (من قبلكم) attached to an adjective of أمم «[Note: or attached to (كذّب).]» (الواو) a conjunction (ما) a negation, disregarded (على الرسول) attached to a fronted predicate (إلّا) for restriction (البلاغ) a delayed subject, nominative.
Clause: «إن تكذّبوا ...» is in the position of an accusative, conjoined to the clause of the quoted speech «[Note: it is said that this speech up to His saying: «عذاب أليم» - verse 23 - is from the speech of Muḥammad, peace be upon him, a parenthesis in the story of Abraham.]».
Clause: «قد كذّب أمم ...» has no grammatical position; it is a justification of the implied apodosis, that is: "if you deny, your denial does not harm me, because nations have denied before you ..."
Clause: «ما على الرسول ...» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause قد كذّب ...

* Rhetoric:
Indefiniteness: in the saying of the Exalted لا يَمْلِكُونَ لَكُمْ رِزْقاً:
He made الرزق indefinite and then definite, because he meant: "they are not able to provide you with any provision at all; so seek the provision from Allah, for He alone is the Provider, and no other provides."

safi-cedvel:19-19.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) for the interrogative of denial (الواو) a conjunction (كيف) an interrogative noun in the position of an accusative, a ḥāl, its governing word being يبدئ (ثم) a particle of resumption «[Note: Professor ʿAbbās Ḥasan said in his book (al-Naḥw al-Wāfī): "It is not permissible that (ثمّ) here be a conjunction, because the repetition of creation has not occurred, so how could they acknowledge seeing it? What confirms that it is for resumption is His saying after that: Say: Travel in the land and see how He began creation; then Allah brings the last creation into being. It is impossible that they travel and see the beginning of creation and then the bringing into being of the last creation …" (end, abridged …) The i'rab scholars have unconvincing interpretations to establish the conjunction, and Professor ʿAbbās Ḥasan's opinion agrees with the opinion of Ibn Hishām in al-Mughnī.]», (على الله) attached to يسير.
Clause: «لم يروا ...» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to an implied resumption, that is:
"Were they heedless and did they not see ..."
Clause: «يبدئ الله ...» is in the position of an accusative, a direct object of the verb of seeing, which is suspended by the interrogative كيف.
Clause: «يعيده ...» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
Clause: «إنّ ذلك ... يسير ...» has no grammatical position; it is a justification.

safi-cedvel:20-20.t:
* I'rab:
(في الأرض) attached to (سيروا), (الفاء) a conjunction (كيف بدأ ...) like كيف يبدئ «[Note: in the preceding verse (19).]», (ثمّ) a particle of resumption (النشأة) mafʿūl muṭlaq standing in for the maṣdar because it is its fellow in derivation, accusative (على كلّ) attached to قدير.
Clause: «قل ...» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
Clause: «سيروا ...» is in the position of an accusative, being the quoted speech.
Clause: «انظروا ...» is in the position of an accusative, conjoined to the quoted speech.
Clause: «بدأ الخلق ...» is in the position of an accusative, a direct object, and the verb of looking is suspended by the interrogative كيف.
Clause: «الله ينشئ ...» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
Clause: «ينشئ ...» is in the position of a nominative, the predicate of the subject (لله).
Clause: «إنّ الله ... قدير» has no grammatical position; it is a justification.

* Morphology:
(النشأة): a noun of the maṣdar (ism maṣdar) of the quadriliteral أنشأ, or it is the maṣdar of the triliteral نشأ of the fatḥ class, or نشؤ of the karuma class.. There are other maṣdars of the triliteral: نشأ - with fatḥa then sukūn - and نشوء - with ḍamma on the nūn - and نشاء and نشاءة - with fatḥa on the nūn - and the wazn of النشأة is فعلة with fatḥa then sukūn, and it is to be noted that it is on the wazn of the maṣdar of single occurrence (maṣdar al-marra).

* Rhetoric:
Pronoun and explicit noun (al-iḍmār wa-l-iẓhār): in the saying of the Exalted فَانْظُرُوا كَيْفَ بَدَأَ الْخَلْقَ ثُمَّ اللَّهُ يُنْشِئُ النَّشْأَةَ الْآخِرَةَ» for someone may say: What is the meaning of stating His name explicitly while making it the subject in His saying «ثُمَّ اللَّهُ يُنْشِئُ النَّشْأَةَ الْآخِرَةَ» after having used a pronoun for it in His saying «كَيْفَ بَدَأَ الْخَلْقَ»? The analogy would be to say: "see how Allah began creation, then brings the last creation into being." The answer: Since the restoration was, in their view, among the great matters, and the opening of the speech was addressed to them regarding the beginning, and it was established for them that this is from Allah, He argued against them that restoration is a bringing into being like the beginning; and if Allah, whom nothing overwhelms, is the One whom the beginning did not overwhelm, then He is the One whom the restoration must not overwhelm. It is as if He had said: "Then the One who brought the first creation into being is the One who brings the last creation into being." So to indicate and alert to this meaning, He brought His name out and made it the subject.

safi-cedvel:21-21.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) a conjunction (إليه) attached to (تقلبون), and the (الواو) in it is the deputy agent.
Clause: «يعذّب ...» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive «[Note: it may be a second predicate of the subject, the name of Majesty, in the preceding verse.]».
Clause: «يشاء ...» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the first relative (من).
Clause: «يرحم ...» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause يعذّب.
Clause: «يشاء (the second)» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the second relative (من).
Clause: «تقلبون ...» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause يعذّب.

safi-cedvel:65-66.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) is resumptive. (في الفلك) is attached to (ركبوا). (دعوا) is a past verb, built on the ḍamma implied on the alif that was dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters; and the (الواو) is the fāʿil (agent). (مخلصين) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil of (دعوا). (له) is attached to (مخلصين) [Note: or attached to a ḥāl from (الدين).]. (الدين) is the direct object of the active participle. (الفاء) is a conjunction. (لمّا) is an adverb meaning "when" (ḥīna), containing the sense of a condition, in the position of accusative, attached to the content of the apodosis. (إلى البرّ) is attached to (نجّاهم). (إذا) is the particle of suddenness (fujāʾiyya)..
The clause «ركبوا ... » is in the position of genitive, a muḍāf ilayhi.
And the clause «دعوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
And the clause «نجّاهم..» is in the position of genitive, a muḍāf ilayhi.
And the clause «هم يشركون..» has no grammatical position; it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
And the clause «يشركون..» is in the position of nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هم).
(66) (اللام) is the lām of consequence (lām al-ʿāqiba). (يكفروا) is an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied (أن) after the lām, and likewise (ليتمتّعوا). (بما) is attached to (يكفروا). (الفاء) is resumptive. (سوف) is a particle of futurity. And the interpreted maṣdar (أن يكفروا..) is in the position of genitive by the lām, attached to (يشركون).
And the interpreted maṣdar (أن يتمتّعوا..) is in the position of genitive by the lām, attached to (يشركون), being conjoined to the first maṣdar.
And the clause «يكفروا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the particle-type relative (the implied (أن)).
And the clause «آتيناهم....» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (ما) [Note: and the returning pronoun is omitted, its implied form being "إيّاه", and it is the second direct object.].
And the clause «يتمتّعوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the second implied particle-type (أن).
And the clause «سوف يعلمون ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.

* Rhetoric:
Figurative usage (al-majāz): in the saying of Allah the Exalted «لِيَكْفُرُوا بِما آتَيْناهُمْ وَلِيَتَمَتَّعُوا فَسَوْفَ يَعْلَمُونَ».
If you ask: how can it be permissible for Allah the Exalted to command disbelief, and that the disobedient do what they please, when He forbids that and threatens punishment for it? The answer: it is a figurative expression for abandonment and forsaking, and that this command is extremely displeasing. An example: you see a man who has resolved on a matter, and in your view the matter is mistaken and will lead to great harm; you go to great lengths in advising him and getting him to come down from his opinion, but when you see nothing from him but refusal and determination, you become angry with him and say: "You and your affair; do what you like", and by this you do not intend the real meaning of the command.

* Benefits:
1- Human types in the Book of Allah are many, such as:
- إِنَّ الْإِنْسانَ خُلِقَ هَلُوعاً.
- وخلق الإنسان جزوعا.
- وخلق الإنسان عجولا.
- وَخُلِقَ الْإِنْسانُ ضَعِيفاً.
In this verse that we are dealing with, the Noble Qur'an depicts for us the human being: how he resorts to Allah at the time of need and at the time of distress, until, when what he is in is removed from him, he forgets Allah and turns away, and denies His favours and kindnesses..
2- Al-Khalīl ibn Aḥmad counted the lāms, and they reached forty-one lāms; we count them one by one, and they are: the lām of oath, the lām of the response to the oath, the lām of command, the lām of the response to the command, the lām of promise, the lām of threat, the lām of emphasis, the lām of support, the lām of denial (lām al-juḥūd), the lām of kay (purpose), the lām of the light inna, the lām of limit, the lām of hope, the lām of wish, the lām of warning, the lām of praise, the lām of blame, the lām of kamā, the lām of the transferred, the lām of requital, the lām of intercession, the lām of appeal for help, the lām of the genitive, the lām of description, the lām of the origin, the lām of definiteness, the lām of multiplicity, the lām of commencement, the lām of preference, the lām of laysa, the lām of negation, the lām of ghayr, the lām of exoneration, the lām of the connection, the lām of prohibition, the lām of supplication, the lām of entitlement, the lām of adjunction, the lām of eloquence. [Translator's note: the list as given in the source contains thirty-nine names, not forty-one.] These lāms are divided into three kinds:
operating the genitive, operating the jussive, and non-operating.

safi-cedvel:67-68.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) is for the interrogation of rebuke (istifhām inkārī). (الواو) is a conjunction. (أنّا) is a particle resembling the verb and its ism (noun). (حرما) is a second direct object.. and the first object is omitted, i.e. "their land" or "Mecca". (الواو) is the wāw of ḥāl. (الناس) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), nominative. (من حولهم) is attached to (يتخطّف). (الهمزة) is like the first. (الفاء) is a conjunction. (بالباطل) is attached to (يؤمنون). (بنعمة) is attached to (يكفرون).
The clause «لم يروا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to an implied resumption, i.e.: "Were they heedless, and did they not see ...".
And the clause «جعلنا ... » is in the position of nominative, the khabar of (أنّ).
And the interpreted maṣdar (أنّا جعلنا ... ) is in the position of accusative, standing in the place of the two objects of (يروا).
And the clause «يتخطّف الناس ... » is in the position of accusative, a ḥāl (circumstantial).
And the clause «يؤمنون..» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause «لم يروا».
And the clause «يكفرون..» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause «يؤمنون».
(68) (الواو) is a conjunction. (من) is an interrogative noun in the position of nominative, a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is (أظلم). (ممّن) is attached to (أظلم). (على الله) is attached to (افترى). (كذبا) is a direct object, accusative [Note: or an absolute object (mafʿūl muṭlaq) standing in for the maṣdar, being its synonym, the object being omitted.]. (بالحقّ) is attached to (كذّب). (لمّا جاءه) is like (لمّا نجّاهم) [Note: in verse (65) of this sūra.]. (الهمزة) is for the interrogation of affirmation (istifhām taqrīrī), because it has entered upon a negation, although it contains in origin the sense of rebuke. (في جهنّم) is attached to the khabar of (ليس). (مثوى) is the ism of (ليس), postponed, nominative, its sign of nominative being the implied ḍamma. (للكافرين) is attached to an adjective (naʿt) of (مثوى) ...
And the clause «من أظلم....» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the resumptive clause "Were they heedless..".
And the clause «افترى ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (من).
And the clause «كذّب ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the ṣila clause.
And the clause «جاءه ... » is in the position of genitive, a muḍāf ilayhi ... and the apodosis of the condition is omitted, what precedes it indicating it.
And the clause «ليس في جهنّم مثوى..» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.

safi-cedvel:69-69.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive. (فينا) is attached to (جاهدوا), with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "in our way". (اللام) is the lām of an oath, for an implied oath. (نهدينهم) is an imperfect verb built on fatḥa, in the position of nominative; the fāʿil (agent) is "we", of magnification, and (هم) is a pronoun, a direct object. (سبلنا) is a second direct object, accusative. (الواو) is a conjunction. (اللام) is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa) of emphasis. (مع) is an accusative adverb attached to the khabar of (إنّ).
The clause «الذين جاهدوا.....» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause «جاهدوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
And the clause «نهدينّهم ... » has no grammatical position; it is the response to the implied oath ...
And the implied oath clause is in the position of nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الذين) [Note: or the khabar is omitted, the response to the oath indicating it.].
And the clause «إنّ الله لمع المحسنين» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the resumptive clause.

* Rhetoric:
Concision by omission (al-ījāz bi-l-ḥadhf): in the saying of Allah the Exalted «وَالَّذِينَ جاهَدُوا فِينا». He left striving unrestricted and did not qualify it with an object, so as to include everything that must be striven against: the soul that commands evil, Satan, and the enemies of the religion.

safi-cedvel:22-22.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (ما أنتم بمعجزين) like ما هم بحاملين «[Note: in verse (12) of this sūra.]», (في الأرض) attached to a ḥāl of the pronoun in معجزين (لا) redundant, to emphasise the negation (في السماء) attached to what (في الأرض) is attached to, so it is conjoined to it (الواو) a conjunction (ما) a negation, disregarded (لكم) attached to a fronted predicate (من دون) attached to a ḥāl of (وليّ), which is genitive in form, nominative in position, a delayed subject (الواو) a conjunction (لا) redundant, to emphasise the negation (نصير) conjoined to وليّ, nominative in position, genitive in form.
Clause: «ما أنتم بمعجزين ...» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
Clause: «ما لكم ... من وليّ ...» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the resumptive clause.

safi-cedvel:23-23.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) a conjunction (بآيات) attached to (كفروا), (أولئك) a demonstrative noun, a second subject in the position of a nominative (من رحمتي) attached to (يئسوا), (لهم) attached to the fronted predicate of the subject عذاب ...
Clause: «الذين كفروا ...» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause ما أنتم بمعجزين «[Note: in the preceding verse (22).]».
Clause: «كفروا ...» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative (الذين).
Clause: «أولئك يئسوا ...» is in the position of a nominative, the predicate of the subject (الذين).
Clause: «يئسوا ...» is in the position of a nominative, the predicate of the subject (أولئك).
Clause: «أولئك لهم عذاب» is in the position of a nominative, conjoined to the clause أولئك يئسوا.
Clause: «لهم عذاب ...» is in the position of a nominative, the predicate of the second subject (أولئك).

safi-cedvel:24-24.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) resumptive «[Note: a return to the story of Abraham, peace be upon him.. or the fāʾ is a conjunction, and what lies between the conjoined and the word it is conjoined to is a parenthetical.]», (ما) a negation (جواب) predicate of كان (إلّا) for restriction (أن) a maṣdar particle.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن قالوا ...) is in the position of a nominative, the delayed subject (ism) of كان.
(أو) a conjunction, and likewise (الفاء) (من النار) attached to (أنجاه), (في ذلك) attached to the predicate of إنّ (اللام) for emphasis (آيات) the ism of إنّ, accusative, and the sign of the accusative is the kasra (لقوم) attached to an adjective of آيات.
Clause: «كان جواب قومه..» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
Clause: «قالوا ...» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the particle-type relative (أن).
Clause: «اقتلوه ...» is in the position of an accusative, being the quoted speech.
Clause: «حرّقوه ...» is in the position of an accusative, conjoined to the clause of the quoted speech.
Clause: «أنجاه الله» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to an implied clause, that is: "so they threw him, and Allah saved him".
Clause: «إنّ في ذلك لآيات ...» has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption.
Clause: «يؤمنون ...» is in the position of a genitive, an adjective of قوم..

safi-cedvel:25-27.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (إنّما) restraining and restrained «[Note: some i'rab scholars made (ما) a maṣdar particle, and the interpreted maṣdar (ما اتّخذتم) in the position of an accusative, the ism of إنّ, with the predicate omitted, that is: "Your taking idols as affection between you will not benefit you".]», (من دون) attached to an omitted second direct object (مودّة) object of purpose, accusative (بينكم) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; latitude has been allowed in the adverb (في الحياة) attached to (اتّخذتم) «[Note: or attached to مودّة.]», (ثمّ) a conjunction (يوم) an accusative adverb of time attached to (يكفر), and likewise (ببعض), (الواو) a conjunction in all three places (ما لكم من ناصرين) like ما لكم.. من وليّ «[Note: in verse (22) of the sūra.]».
Clause: «قال ...» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
