Clause: «اتّخذتم ...» is in the position of an accusative, being the quoted speech.
Clause: «يكفر بعضكم ...» is in the position of an accusative, conjoined to the clause اتّخذتم.
Clause: «يلعن بعضكم ...» is in the position of an accusative, conjoined to the clause اتخذتم.
Clause: «مأواكم النار» is in the position of an accusative, conjoined to the clause اتّخذتم.
Clause: «ما لكم من ناصرين» is in the position of an accusative, conjoined to the clause اتّخذتم.
(26) (الفاء) a conjunction (له) attached to (آمن), (إلى ربّي) attached to مهاجر, and the yāʾ of the first person refers to Abraham «[Note: this is the opinion of the majority; some exegetes say it refers to Lot, peace be upon him.]», (هو) a detached pronoun in the position of a nominative, a subject, its predicate being (العزيز), (الحكيم) a second predicate, nominative.
Clause: «آمن له لوط..» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause قال..
Clause: «قال ...» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause آمن.
Clause: «إنّي مهاجر ...» is in the position of an accusative, being the quoted speech.
Clause: «إنّه هو العزيز..» has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption.
Clause: «هو العزيز ...» is in the position of a nominative, the predicate of إنّ.
(27) (الواو) a conjunction (له) attached to (وهبنا) «[Note: وهب المال فلانا ولفلان - "he gave the property to so-and-so", either directly or with the preposition.]», (في ذريّته) attached to an omitted second direct object, its governing word being جعلنا (في الدنيا) attached to (آتيناه), (في الآخرة) attached to الصالحين (من الصالحين) attached to the predicate of إنّ, and (اللام) is the shifted lām.
Clause: «وهبنا ...» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause قال.
Clause: «وجعلنا ...» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause وهبنا.
Clause: «آتيناه ...» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause وهبنا.
Clause: «إنّه ... من الصالحين» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause آتيناه.

* Benefits:
- His saying, the Exalted, إِنَّمَا اتَّخَذْتُمْ: Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "ما" is parsed in three ways:
a- That it has the meaning of الذي, and the ʿāʾid is omitted, that is "you took it"; and «أوثانا» is a second direct object or a ḥāl, and «مودة» a predicate according to the reading of those who read it in the nominative.
b- That it is a restraining particle (kāffa), and أوثانا is an object, and مودة an object of purpose in the case of the accusative, and in the nominative by the implication of a subject.
c- That «ما» be a maṣdar particle, and مودة a predicate in the case of the nominative, and the implied form is: "the reason for your taking is affection".

safi-cedvel:28-29.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) a conjunction (لوطا) conjoined to إبراهيم - or نوح - accusative «[Note: or a direct object of an omitted verb, its implied form being (اذكر), and the conjunction is a conjunction of clauses.]», (إذ) an adverb in the position of an accusative, attached to the implied verb أرسلنا «[Note: or it is a badal ishtimāl from (لوطا) if it is governed by (اذكر).]», (لقومه) attached to (قال), (اللام) the shifted lām, for emphasis (بها) attached to a ḥāl of the pronoun object, that is: "clothed in it" (أحد) genitive in form, nominative in position, agent of سبقكم (من العالمين) attached to an adjective of أحد.
Clause: «قال ...» is in the position of a genitive, a muḍāf ilayhi.
Clause: «إنّكم لتأتون ...» is in the position of an accusative, being the quoted speech «[Note: or resumptive within the scope of the quoted speech, with no grammatical position.]».
Clause: «تأتون الفاحشة ...» is in the position of a nominative, the predicate of إنّ.
Clause: «ما سبقكم بها من أحد ...» is in the position of an accusative, a ḥāl of الفاحشة or of the agent.
(29) (الهمزة) for the interrogative of denial (إنّكم لتأتون الرجال) like إنّكم لتأتون الفاحشة (الواو) a conjunction in both places (الفاء) resumptive (في ناديكم) attached to a ḥāl of المنكر «[Note: or attached to (تأتون).]», (ما كان ... قالوا) like the first preceding one «[Note: in verse (24) of this sūra.]», (بعذاب) attached to (ائتنا) (كنت) a past verb in the position of a jussive, the protasis (من الصادقين) attached to the predicate of كنت.
Clause: «إنّكم لتأتون ... (the second)» is in the position of an accusative, a badal for the clause إنّكم لتأتون الفاحشة.
Clause: «تأتون الرجال ...» is in the position of a nominative, the predicate of إنّ.
Clause: «تقطعون ...» is in the position of a nominative, conjoined to the clause تأتون الرجال.
Clause: «تأتون ... المنكر» is in the position of a nominative, conjoined to the clause تأتون الرجال.
Clause: «ما كان جواب ...» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
Clause: قالوا ...» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the particle-type relative (أن).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن قالوا ...) is in the position of a nominative, the delayed ism of كان.
Clause: «ائتنا ...» is in the position of an accusative, being the quoted speech.
Clause: «كنت من الصادقين» has no grammatical position; it is a resumption within the scope of the quoted speech ... and the apodosis is omitted, indicated by what precedes it.

* Benefits:
- The clause that is in the position of a genitive:
It is of three kinds:
a- The clause that occurs after an adverb: it is in the position of a genitive by annexation (iḍāfa), like the clause we are dealing with, namely: ولوطا إذ قال لقومه, for the adverb «إذ» has been annexed to the clause «قال».
b- The clause that occurs as an adjective of a genitive noun, like "Read in a book whose handwriting is clear": the clause «خطه واضح», consisting of a subject and predicate, is in the position of a genitive, an adjective of الكتاب.
c- The clause that follows a clause in the position of a genitive, whether conjoined, substitutive or emphatic, like "The teacher, if he advises the students and warns them, is sincere to them": the clause وحذرهم is conjoined to the clause نصح, which is in the position of a genitive, so it too is genitive.
- What stands in for the agent is four things:
a- The direct object: it is the foundation and the head, like قضي الأمر.
b- The noun governed by a preposition, like «لَمَّا سُقِطَ فِي أَيْدِيهِمْ».
c- The inflected adverb (al-ẓarf al-mutaṣarrif), which is what the predication may validly be assigned to, such as: day, night, month, year, ʿām, age, etc.: like صيم رمضان, ومشي يوم, وقعد ليلة.
d- The inflected specified maṣdar, like: فَإِذا نُفِخَ فِي الصُّورِ نَفْخَةٌ واحِدَةٌ.

safi-cedvel:30-30.t:
* I'rab:
(ربّ) a vocative, a muḍāf, accusative, and the sign of the accusative is the implied fatḥa on its last letter ... and the (ياء), omitted for lightness, is the muḍāf ilayhi (على القوم) attached to (انصرني).
Clause: «قال ...» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
Clause of the vocative and its response ... is in the position of an accusative, being the quoted speech.
Clause: «انصرني ...» has no grammatical position; it is the response to the vocative.

safi-cedvel:31-31.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (لمّا) an adverb with the sense of "when", containing the sense of a condition, in the position of an accusative, attached to the apodosis قالوا (بالبشرى) attached to a ḥāl of the agent of جاءت or of its object (إنّا) a particle resembling the verb (inna), and its ism is (القرية) a badal for هذه - or an ʿaṭf bayān -.
Clause: «جاءت رسلنا ...» is in the position of a genitive, a muḍāf ilayhi.
Clause: «قالوا ...» has no grammatical position; it is the apodosis of a non-jussive conditional.
Clause: «إنّا مهلكو ...» is in the position of an accusative, being the quoted speech.
Clause: «إنّ أهلها كانوا ...» has no grammatical position; it is a justification.
Clause: «كانوا ظالمين» is in the position of a nominative, the predicate of إنّ.

safi-cedvel:32-32.t:
* I'rab:
(فيها) attached to the predicate of إنّ (بمن) attached to أعلم (اللام) the lām of the oath, for an implied oath (ننجّينّه) an imperfect verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of a nominative (أهله) conjoined to the pronoun object (in ننجّينّه), accusative (إلّا) a particle of exception (امرأته) accusative as the excepted (من الغابرين) attached to the predicate of كانت.
Clause: «قال ...» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
Clause: «إنّ فيها لوطا ...» is in the position of an accusative, being the quoted speech.
Clause: «قالوا ...» has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption.
Clause: «نحن أعلم ...» is in the position of an accusative, being the quoted speech.
Clause: «ننجّينّه ...» has no grammatical position; it is the response to the implied oath ... and the clause of the implied oath has no grammatical position; it is a resumption within the scope of the quoted speech.
Clause: «كانت من الغابرين ...» has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption.

* Rhetoric:
The art of allusion (fann al-ishāra): in the saying of the Exalted إِنَّ فِيها لُوطاً.
The aim is not to inform them that he is in it, but rather it is a dispute about his case: for when they justified the destruction of its people by their wrongdoing, he objected to them that in it was one who was free of wrongdoing. By the dispute he intended to show compassion for them, and what is due from a believer, grieving for his brother, bestirring himself to support and protect him, and fearing that harm touch him or injury reach him. This is among the eloquent and subtle allusions.

safi-cedvel:38-38.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (عادا) a direct object of an omitted verb, its implied form being (أهلكنا), and the agent of (تبيّن) is a latent pronoun referring to the destruction understood from the context of the verse (لكم) attached to (تبيّن), (من مساكنهم) attached to (تبيّن), (الواو) the wāw of ḥāl - or resumptive (لهم) attached to (زيّن), (الفاء) a conjunction (عن السبيل) attached to (ضدّهم), (الواو) the wāw of ḥāl.
Clause: « (أهلكنا) ...» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
Clause: «تبيّن ... (إهلاكهم)» has no grammatical position; it is parenthetical «[Note: or in the position of an accusative, a ḥāl.]».
Clause: «زيّن لهم الشيطان ...» is in the position of an accusative, a ḥāl, with (قد) implied «[Note: or has no grammatical position, being resumptive.]».
Clause: «صدّهم ...» is in the position of an accusative, conjoined to the clause زيّن لهم الشيطان.
Clause: «كانوا مستبصرين» is in the position of an accusative, a ḥāl, with (قد) implied.

* Morphology:
(مستبصرين), plural of مستبصر, an active participle from the sextriliteral (sudāsī) استبصر; its wazn is مستفعل with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn.

safi-cedvel:39-39.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) a conjunction in all three places (قارون) conjoined to (عادا) «[Note: in the preceding verse (38).]», (الواو) resumptive (لقد جاءهم موسى) like لقد تركنا «[Note: in verse (35) of this sūra.]», (بالبيّنات) attached to a ḥāl of موسى (الفاء) a conjunction (في الأرض) attached to (استكبروا) (الواو) a conjunction (ما) a negation.
Clause: «جاءهم موسى ...» has no grammatical position; it is the response to the implied oath ...
The clause of the implied oath has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
Clause: «استكبروا ...» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the response to the oath.
Clause: «ما كانوا سابقين» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the response to the oath.

safi-cedvel:40-40.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) resumptive (كلّا) a fronted direct object, accusative (بذنبه) attached to (أخذنا), and the bāʾ expresses cause (الفاء) a conjunction of consequence (tafrīʿ) (منهم) attached to a fronted predicate of the delayed subject (من أرسلنا) «[Note: it may be an adjective of an omitted subject, its implied form being "some of them", in which case the predicate is the relative.]», (عليه) attached to (أرسلنا), and the following similar clauses are parsed likewise (به) attached to (خسفنا), (الواو) a conjunction (ما) a negation (اللام) the lām of denial (juḥūd) or disavowal (يظلمهم) an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after the lām (الواو) a conjunction (أنفسهم) a fronted direct object.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يظلمهم ...) is in the position of a genitive by the lām, attached to an omitted predicate of كان.
Clause: «أخذنا ...» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
Clause: «منهم من أرسلنا ...» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the resumptive clause.
Clause: «أرسلنا ...» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the first relative (من).
Clause: «منهم من أخذته ...» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause منهم من أرسلنا.
Clause: «أخذته الصيحة ...» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the second relative (من).
Clause: «منهم من خسفنا ...» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause منهم من أرسلنا.
Clause: «خسفنا ...» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the third relative (من).
Clause: «منهم من أغرقنا ...» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause منهم من أرسلنا.
Clause: «أغرقنا ...» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the fourth relative (من).
Clause: «ما كان الله ...» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the resumptive clause.
Clause: «يظلمهم ...» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the implied particle-type relative (أن).
Clause: «كانوا ... يظلمون ...» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause ما كان الله ليظلمهم.
Clause: «يظلمون» is in the position of an accusative, the predicate of كانوا.

* Benefits:
- كلا is a fronted direct object of the verb «أخذنا ...»; we have already spoken of كل and بعض earlier.
- وَما كانَ اللَّهُ لِيَظْلِمَهُمْ: this lām is the lām of denial (lām al-juḥūd), whose definition is that it is preceded by a negated كون, and it has already been discussed.

safi-cedvel:33-35.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (لمّا ... لوطا) like لمّا ...
إبراهيم «[Note: in verse (31) of this sūra.]», (أن) redundant, and the deputy agent of the verb (سيء) is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "هو" (he), that is Lot «[Note: it is permissible that the pronoun refer to the maṣdar of the verb, with the sense "distress came to him".]», (بهم) attached to (سيء), and the bāʾ expresses cause (بهم) the second, attached to (ضاق) (ذرعا) a specification (tamyīz), accusative, transformed from an agent, that is: "his capacity was constrained by them" (الواو) a conjunction in all three places (لا) a prohibitive that jusses, in both places (إنّا منجّوك) like إنّا مهلكو ..., (أهلك) a direct object of an omitted verb, its implied form being "we will save" «[Note: this is according to the opinion of Sībawayh; al-Akhfash permits the conjoining of the noun to the position of the kāf in (منّجوك), because its position is genitive and accusative.]», (إلّا ... الغابرين) like إلّا امرأته كانت من الغابرين «[Note: in verse (32) of this sūra.]».
Clause: «جاءت رسلنا ...» is in the position of a genitive, a muḍāf ilayhi.
Clause: «سيء بهم ...» has no grammatical position; it is the apodosis of a non-jussive conditional.
Clause: «ضاق بهم ...» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause سيء بهم.
Clause: «قالوا ...» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause سيء بهم.
Clause: «لا تخف ...» is in the position of an accusative, being the quoted speech.
Clause: «لا تحزن ...» is in the position of an accusative, conjoined to the clause of the quoted speech.
Clause: «إنّا منجّوك ...» has no grammatical position; it is a justification.
Clause: «كانت من الغابرين» has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption.
(34) (إنّا) a particle resembling the verb, and its ism (على أهل) attached to (منزلون), (جزاء) a direct object of the active participle منزلون (من السماء) attached to an adjective of (رجزا), (ما) a maṣdar particle ...
The interpreted maṣdar (ما كانوا ...) is in the position of a genitive by the bāʾ, attached to the active participle منزلون, and the bāʾ expresses cause.
Clause: «إنّا منزلون ...» has no grammatical position; it is a justification of the saving.
Clause: «كانوا يفسقون» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the particle-type relative (ما).
Clause: «يفسقون» is in the position of an accusative, the predicate of كانوا.
(35) (الواو) a conjunction (اللام) the lām of the oath, for an implied oath (منها) attached to (تركنا), (لقوم) attached to بيّنة «[Note: it may be attached to (تركنا), or to آية.]».
Clause: «تركنا» has no grammatical position; it is the response to the implied oath.
Clause: «يعقلون» is in the position of a genitive, an adjective of قوم.

* Morphology:
(سيء): apparently the alif was changed to yāʾ for conformity with the passive form; its origin was ساء. But the change occurred on the wāw; its imperfect is يسوء, so the origin of the word in the passive was سوئ with ḍamma on the sīn and kasra on the wāw; then the wāw was made sākin because of the heaviness of the kasra and the kasra was moved to the sīn; then the wāw was changed to yāʾ because what precedes it is kasra, and it became سيء. This is the way of the hollow verb whose middle letter is wāw.

safi-cedvel:36-37.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) a conjunction - or resumptive - (إلى مدين) attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being "We sent" (شعيبا) an ʿaṭf bayān - or a badal - accusative (الفاء) a conjunction (قوم) a vocative, a muḍāf, accusative, and the sign of the accusative is the implied fatḥa on what precedes the yāʾ, omitted for lightness ... and the (الياء) is the muḍāf ilayhi (الواو) a conjunction in both places (لا) a prohibitive that jusses (في الأرض) attached to the verb تعثوا (مفسدين) a confirmatory ḥāl, accusative, and the sign of the accusative is the yāʾ.
Clause: « (أرسلنا) ... شعيبا» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause of the implied oath «[Note: in the preceding verse (35), or it is resumptive.]».
Clause: «قال» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause أرسلنا.
The clause of the vocative and its response is in the position of an accusative, being the quoted speech.
Clause: «اعبدوا ...» has no grammatical position; it is the response to the vocative.
Clause: «ارجوا ...» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the response to the vocative.
Clause: «لا تعثوا ...» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the response to the vocative.
(37) (الفاء) a conjunction in all three places (في دارهم) attached to (جاثمين), the predicate of أصبحوا.
Clause: «كذّبوه ...» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause قال.
Clause: «أخذتهم الرجفة ...» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause كذّبوه.
Clause: «أصبحوا ... جاثمين» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause أخذتهم الرجفة.
